The Institution of Electrical Engineers, The Association of Consulting Engineers, The Elec- trical Contractors' Association of Scotland, The Electrical Association for Women, The National Farmers' Union. Electrical Installation Contractors holding the Certificate of the National Register have given evidence of competency; their work is subject to periodical inspection; they undertake to pay rates of wages and observe conditions of em- ployment not less favourable than those of the appropriate trade agreement; and observe the Regulations for the Electrical Equipment of Buildings issued by the Institution of Electrical Engineers.

brief_context: Ceded territory where Finland lost its largest generating station.
brief_extract:
Power Supply
Despite the number of lakes there is not an abundant supply of hydro-electric power, for Finland is a country of small rainfall, low elevation and fluctuating water flows-physical difficulties overcome by engineering skill, but at considerable cost. Moreover, production dropped by one-third in 1945 due to the loss of the largest generating station in the ceded territory of the Karelia. Nevertheless the electricity authorities courageously designed power plant projects of ambitious dimensions.

article_title: A Kentish Hop Garden —Yesterday and Today
brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE APRIL, 1955
A Kentish Hop Garden
—Yesterday and Today
By JOAN BATCHELOR
Most of us know only of hop growing from a fleeting glimpse through a train or car window at avenues of graceful green garlands which by some transformation produce an amber liquid. A talk to Medway Branch on electricity’s part in the process sounded so interesting that we thought that ELECTRICAL AGE readers would like to know something first-hand from a family hop garden. Typical oast houses in a Kentish hop garden
The Brewers' Society
A FULL description of the hop-growing industry would be as long as an ordinary novel, and I will therefore pick out the special points of interest in the use of electrical equipment.

THE buildings of ancient Rome such as the Colosseum and the Pantheon, which have stood for nearly 2,000 years, have some- thing to teach us in our technical present. brief_extract: Last year we had two million tons of a waste substance, which, properly treated, could give the enduring properties of these Roman buildings as well as affording other advantages. article_title: Advertisement: National Register of Electrical Installation Contractors - The value of Confidence
brief_extract: The National Register of Electrical Installation Contractors, established over 30 years ago, aims at maintaining a high standard of qualification and raising the efficiency and status of Electrical Installation Contractors, thereby safeguarding the public against inferior materials and workmanship. The National Register of Electrical Installation Contractors is an independent body directed by representatives of important Associations interested in electrical installation work, including The Institution of Electrical Engineers, The Association of Consulting Engineers, The Electrical Contractors' Association of Scotland, The Electrical Association for Women, The National Farmers' Union. Electrical Installation Contractors holding the Certificate of the National Register have given evidence of competency; their work is subject to periodical inspection; they undertake to pay rates of wages and observe conditions of employment not less favourable than those of the appropriate trade agreement; and observe the Regulations for the Electrical Equipment of Buildings issued by the Institution of Electrical Engineers.

brief_context: Town near the centre of Rochester where homes are.
article_title: Interesting Events in E.A.W. Branches: VISIT TO OLD PEOPLE'S HOMES
brief_extract: At present the County Council is providing in these various ways for about 2,200 old people and there is a waiting list of about 450 other aged men and women whose need for admission to homes is accepted. The Medway Homes comprise seven separate self-contained villas grouped around a green in an estate which, though secluded, is near the centre of Rochester and Chatham. The accommodation is for 160 old people.

brief_context: Town mentioned as being near Darenth Grange.
brief_extract: Darenth Grange is an example of a more rural home, although it is not far from the town of Dartford. Formerly a private residence, it was adapted and opened in 1951 to accommodate 48 men and women.

brief_context: A residential complex for the elderly described on the page.
brief_extract: The homes are run with virtually no rules and regulations, the old people being treated as they would be in a well-conducted private hotel. The Medway Cottage Homes each have an electrical installation comprising lighting, 13 amp. sockets, night lights, night call bells, front and back door bells, central radio, and fire alarm systems.

article_title: VISIT TO RONUK WORKS, PORTSLADE, SUSSEX
brief_extract:
DUMBRELL Hon. Secretary, Eastbourne Branch

Grouped in the handsomely proportioned assembly hall of Ronuk Works, which is hung with fine oil paintings and has a wood floor bearing eloquent testimony to the efficiency of Ronuk polish, we were given some interesting information before starting on our tour of the Works. Ronuk wax polish was known as Fowler's Wax Composition when the founder of the firm, Mr.

brief_context: Mentioned as the origin of carnauba wax.
article_title: VISIT TO RONUK WORKS, PORTSLADE, SUSSEX
brief_extract: containers we saw specially packed for hospital use. The name "Ronuk" which is a translation of an Arabic word, means "brightness" or "shining." Ronuk is very much "animal, vegetable and mineral", being composed of beeswax gathered in tropical forests, carnauba, a wax from Brazilian palms, and paraffin wax. We were shown the huge vats in which the components are mixed with an electrically operated rotary movement to prevent sediment settling.

brief_context: Region mentioned regarding climatic conditions for polish hardness.
article_title: VISIT TO RONUK WORKS, PORTSLADE, SUSSEX
brief_extract: The whole process of filling, cooling and putting on wax paper and lids is powered by electricity. We were told that the polish is made in varying degrees of hardness to suit climatic conditions from Scandinavia to the tropics. The familiar blue tins and metal bottles are packed in wood or cardboard containers, and these are also made by the firm.

brief_context: Region where steel wool mesh is used for arm adornments.
article_title: VISIT TO RONUK WORKS, PORTSLADE, SUSSEX
brief_extract: A subsidiary firm makes Panda steel wool and metal pot scourers. We saw some of the stocking like lengths of mesh from which the latter are made, and our guide told us that these lengths are in great demand in parts of West Africa, where the local belles favour them for arm adornments. Rather scratchy mittens, we thought!

Secretary, Woolwich E.A.W. Branch

THE National Maritime Museum, as its name indicates, covers every aspect of Britain’s life at sea. The Royal Navy naturally figures mainly in the Museum’s galleries, but the history of the Merchant Navy and the Fishing Fleet is also depicted in paintings, photographs and models.

location_standardised: Greenwich, Greater London, England, United Kingdom

brief_extract: The Royal Navy naturally figures mainly in the Museum’s galleries, but the history of the Merchant Navy and the Fishing Fleet is also depicted in paintings, photographs and models. The Museum can boast of the most beautiful setting of any of the country’s national collections, standing as it does between the green slopes of Greenwich Park rising steeply to the old Observatory and Blackheath, and in the north stretching down to the banks of the Thames and the wide lawns and stately buildings of the Royal Naval College, and the Seamen’s Hospital on the site of a 15th Century royal palace. The central building is the Queen’s House, built in 1635 by Inigo Jones.

Miss Mary Graham has been ap- pointed Deputy Consul-General in New York, the first time a British woman has been given such an ap- pointment. ELECTRICITY AND THE FUTURE
In a brilliant Presidential Address to the 1955 British Electrical Power Convention, Sir Harry Railing said that the world demand for electricity had increased at the rate of 7% per annum, and he expected a greater in- crease than 7% in the United King- dom in the near future to meet the demands of heavy engineering and capital goods, of transport, and of agriculture.

brief_context: Location where electricity demand is expected to increase.
Coal was significant to its ascendancy over 150 years.
brief_extract:
Sir Harry said: “It is as important an insurance for any country to stock- pile a certain percentage of plant for energy production as it is to stockpile food or raw materials. The life of every section of industry, indeed that of the nation, depends as much on electric power as it does on food.”
The main sources of fuel supply were coal, oil and nuclear fuel, and for the British Commonwealth, whose ascendancy over the past 150 years had owed so much to coal, a new opportunity arose in the atomic age. Looking to new horizons and new energy resources, Sir Harry said our future research efforts must be dir- ected into two channels — to use not only the fuel resources accumulated in the past, but as far as economically feasible to utilise the energy which reaches us daily from the sun and, if possible, to store this energy.

location_standardised: Birmingham, West Midlands, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of the E.A.W. branch whose members visited Schweppes.
article_title: VISIT TO SCHWEPPES LTD., COLWALL, MALVERN
brief_extract:
A. WALSH, Magazine Secretary, Birmingham Branch
Members visited this little modern
factory in the heart of rural England. Schweppes came to this country from
Switzerland, and have been famous
since 1792.

brief_context: Original country from which Schweppes originated.
article_title: VISIT TO SCHWEPPES LTD., COLWALL, MALVERN
brief_extract:
WALSH, Magazine Secretary, Birmingham Branch
Members visited this little modern
factory in the heart of rural England. Schweppes came to this country from
Switzerland, and have been famous
since 1792. It was very interesting to
watch the all-electric machinery for
the bottling plant in which 600 bottles
per hour are washed in caustic soda
to ensure complete cleanliness.

brief_context: Natural spring that supplies water to the Schweppes factory.
article_title: VISIT TO SCHWEPPES LTD., COLWALL, MALVERN
brief_extract:
All crates are lined with paper
to prevent dust entering the crates. Members visited Primeswell Spring,
which has been known for over a
thousand years, and is mentioned in
Warwick Deeping's Domesday Book. The water from the spring supplies
the factory, and one large tank sup-
plies the factory and keeps it going
for one day.

brief_context: Mentioned as the continent where the refinery is significant.
article_title: VISIT TO KENT OIL REFINERY, ISLE OF GRAIN
brief_extract:
R. Sheldon, Magazine Secretary, Medway Branch

The Kent Oil Refinery of the British Petroleum Company is one of the largest in Europe. It was built since the war, commencing operation in 1953.

brief_context: The river where the refinery's deep water port is located.
article_title: VISIT TO KENT OIL REFINERY, ISLE OF GRAIN
brief_extract: It was built since the war, commencing operation in 1953. The plant covers a little over a square mile and includes a deep water port on the River Medway capable of accepting tankers up to 40,000 tons, 600 miles of pipeline, 22 miles of roads, 5 miles of railway, and a 16-million gallon cooling water reservoir. The refinery processes 4 million tons a year of crude oil from the Middle East, producing motor spirit, diesel oil, kerosene, fuel and lubricating oils.

brief_context: The region where the refinery's crude oil originates.
article_title: VISIT TO KENT OIL REFINERY, ISLE OF GRAIN
brief_extract: The plant covers a little over a square mile and includes a deep water port on the River Medway capable of accepting tankers up to 40,000 tons, 600 miles of pipeline, 22 miles of roads, 5 miles of railway, and a 16-million gallon cooling water reservoir. The refinery processes 4 million tons a year of crude oil from the Middle East, producing motor spirit, diesel oil, kerosene, fuel and lubricating oils. The products are primarily produced by distillation.

brief_context: Location of the carpet factory mentioned in the title.
brief_extract:
Amongst other things printed by Messrs. Holbrook are Weldon's Fashion Books, which were of interest " hot from the press."

VISIT TO "CARPET TRADES" FACTORY, KIDDERMINSTER
By Mrs. B.

brief_context: Branch location where Mrs. B. Trout is Magazine Secretary.
brief_extract:
B. TROUT, Magazine Secretary, Redditch Branch

"Carpet Trades" is the largest, most up-to-date factory in England, and has the trade name of "Meadow." Both Axminster and Wilton carpets are made, as well as felts, knitting yarns for hosiery firms, and the firm's own carpet wools. The telling slogan is " From Sheep to Shop."

Since the making of carpets has its traditions extending over many centuries, during which carpets were hand-made, it was interesting to see the modern method of mass production.
